```{r setup}
library(bioRtools)
library(ggplot2)
```

This workflow uses the public `nutrimouse` lipid dataset distributed with
`mixOmics` (Martin et al., 2007; DOI 10.1002/hep.21510).

```{r data}
data(nutrimouse, package = "mixOmics")

X <- as.data.frame(nutrimouse$lipid)
meta <- data.frame(
  sample = rownames(X),
  diet = nutrimouse$diet,
  genotype = nutrimouse$genotype,
  row.names = rownames(X),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dim(X)
table(meta$diet)
```

## Pairwise OPLS-DA

```{r opls}
set.seed(4)
opls <- suppressWarnings(opls_analysis(
  X,
  sample = meta,
  sample_col = "sample",
  group_col = "diet",
  pairwise = TRUE,
  validation = "CV",
  cv_folds = 4,
  verbose = FALSE
))

class(opls)
head(opls$tables$differential)
```

## Differential metabolite display

```{r volcano}
volcano <- plot_metab_volcano(opls$tables$differential)
volcano
```

## Sparse PLS-DA

```{r spls}
set.seed(9)
fit <- spls_analysis(
  X,
  sample = meta,
  sample_col = "sample",
  group_col = "diet",
  ncomp = 2,
  keep_x = c(10, 5),
  verbose = FALSE
)

fit$tables$variance_explained
fit$plots
```

The native `ropls` and `mixOmics` objects are retained in the `model`
component; the normalized tables and plots are available through the same
`bioRtools_fit` interface.
